NUCLEOSIDES & NUCLEOTIDES, 14(3-5), 337-340 (1995) 
SYNTHESIS OF 9-(2-HYDROXYETHOXYMETHYL)GUANINE 
(ACYCLOVIR) FROM GUANOSINE 
Hiroshi Shiragami, Yoshihito Koguchi, Yasuhiro Tanaka, Satoshi Takamatsu, 
Yumiko Uchida, Takashi Ineyama and Kunisuke Izawa* 
Central Research Laboratories, Ajinomoto Co., Inc. 
1-1 Suzuki-cho, Kawasaki-ku, Kawasaki 210, Japan 
Abstract: A convenient synthesis of 9-(2-hydroxyethoxymethyl)guanine (acyclovir) from 
guanosine by chemical transpurination was developed. The isomerization of the 7-isomer 
to the desired 9-isomer and the purification of the 9-isomer was achieved simply by 
concentration, heating and further crystallization. 
Introduction 
The discovery of 9-(2-hydroxyethoxymethyl)guanine (acyclovir)la-c (1) which has 
potent activity against herpes simplex type 1 and 2 viruses triggered a world wide effort to 
synthesize guanine nucleosides and acyclic nucleoside analogues.2a-f Several methods for 
the synthesis of acyclovir have been reported. Previously, Boryski and Golankiewicz 
reported3 transpurination of tetraa~etylguanosine~ 
(6), leading to 9- and 7-(2- 
acetoxyethoxymethyl)-N2-acetyIguanine (5). However, many problems occur when 
adapting this method for large-scale production, because it requires many steps and 
isolation of intermediary products, and has less regioselectivity. 
Here, we wish to report more convenient and economical synthesis of acyclovir (1) 
from natural g uanos i tie (2) by c hem ical t ran spu ri nat ion. 
Results and Disciission 
Reacting 1,3-dioxolane (3) with acetic anhydride in the presence of acid catalyst 
gave (2-acetoxyethoxy)methyl acetate5 (4). The transpurination reaction of guanosine (2) 
with this acyclic sugar moiety 4 in the presence of acetic anhydride and catalytic amount of 
acid gave a mixture of 9-(2-acetoxyethoxyrnethyl)-N~-acetylguanine 
(5a) and 742- 
acetoxyethoxymethyl)-N2-acetylguanine (5b) in high yield (FIG. I). Various acid catalysts 
were applicable to the transpurination, as summarized in TABLE 1. The reaction proceeded 
with or without solvent.

was stirred at 100 "C under reduced pressure (10 mmHg) for 20 h. The mixture was cooled

route.title: Synthesis of 9-(2-Hydroxyethoxymethyl)guanine (Acyclovir) from Guanosine

steps.notes: Acyclic sugar-moiety synthon used in the subsequent transpurination; no amounts given in text.
steps.evidence: Reacting 1,3-dioxolane (3) with acetic anhydride in the presence of acid catalyst gave (2-acetoxyethoxy)methyl acetate5 (4).

solvents.name: none / solvent-free (reaction proceeded with or without solvent)

conditions.other: Mixture of 9- and 7-isomers obtained in high yield; 9/7-isomer ratio 1.45 by HPLC peak area

steps.yield_value: high yield (not quantified for combined isomers)
steps.notes: TABLE 1 states various acid catalysts were applicable; experimental section text is truncated after reagent charge.
steps.evidence: To 50 g (176.5 mmol) of guanosine were added 62 g (353 mmol) of 4, 180 g (1.75 mol) of acetic anhydride and 3.4 g (17.5 mmol) of p-toluenesulfonic acid

steps.step_label: Concentration and thermal isomerization of 7-isomer (5b) to 9-isomer (5a)

conditions.other: Volatile components removed from reaction mixture, then residue heated under reduced pressure; 9/7 ratio rose from ca. 2.0 to 6.34 (3 h) and 17.1 (22.5 h)

steps.notes: Isomerization conditions milder than previously reported and gave higher N-9/N-7 ratio.
steps.evidence: components from the reaction mixture, followed by heating the residue at 100 °C under reduced pressure ... afforded a much higher N-9/N-7 ratio.

solvents.name: ethyl acetate, acetonitrile or water (appropriate solvent added to residue)

steps.notes: Purification achieved simply by concentration, heating and crystallization.
steps.evidence: by adding an appropriate solvent such as ethyl acetate, acetonitrile or water to the residue, 5a was crystallized selectively from the concentrate (TABLE 2).

steps.step_label: Alkaline deacetylation of 5a and neutralization to acyclovir (1)

conditions.other: Hydrolysis with aq. NaOH followed by neutralization with HCl to precipitate acyclovir

steps.evidence: Treating 5a with aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by neutralization with hydrochloric acid gave acyclovir (I) in 92% yield with high isomeric purity, which means that the overall yield of I from guanosine was 78%.

warnings: The experimental section is truncated in the provided text (procedure for 5a ends at the reagent charge); temperatures/times for step 2 were taken from TABLE 2 process conditions.

The yields '9-isomer (5a) (42%) / 7-isomer (5b) (30%)' in FIG. II appear to refer to the previously reported transpurination of tetraacetylguanosine (6), not to the authors' guanosine procedure; not assigned to a step.
No amounts, temperature or time are given for the preparation of (2-acetoxyethoxy)methyl acetate (4) or for the NaOH/HCl step.
